text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp confirmed Friday that negotiations continue in a dispute over KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV's ownership stake in Northwest.
"We are in discussions with KLM over the ownership dispute between the two companies," Northwest spokesman Doug Killian said.
Earlier, KLM said it was in talks with Northwest to try to resolve a boardroom battle over ownership and to extend an ongoing marketing and operating alliance between the carriers.
Neither KLM nor Northwest would speculate whether talks would lead to KLM selling all or part of its stake in Northwest in exchange for a five to 10-year partnership deal.
Killian said KLM's stake amounts to 19.4 percent of the common stock voting rights of Northwest. The stake dates back to a leveraged buyout at Northwest in 1989.

"(KLM Controller Herman) Bruggink told analysts in Geneva that we were in talks to try to come to an agreement on long-term contracts, and that Northwest wanted to see the dispute between shareholders resolved," KLM spokesman Peter Wellhuner told Reuters in Amsterdam.
Currently, Northwest and KLM have a rolling marketing and operating alliance, allowing either party to withdraw on one year's notice.
"It has been a long stated goal of Northwest Airlines to form a long-term marketing and operating alliance with KLM that would be in the area of five to 10 years," Killian said.
Northwest and KLM began working closely together after receiving antitrust immunity from the U.S. Department of Transportation in 1993, he added.
"KLM has a desire to have a framework of agreement with Northwest Airlines as far as cooperation is concerned over a longer (time) period," Wellhuner said.

The discussions between the two airlines were sparked by two pending lawsuits that KLM filed against Northwest in late 1995. The suits object to NWA's poison pill anti-takeover strategy and to NWA having changed its bylaws to eliminate KLM's ability to veto board decisions.

Since 1993, the NWA-KLM alliance has enabled the two airlines to coordinate their fares, schedules, advertising and purchases from suppliers. In increased revenues and reduced costs, the arrangement is worth about $50 million a year to NWA and $150 million to KLM, Northwest said.
